Be Brave, Be Human, Be Passionate, Be Exceptional.

At Prime these values are integral to who we are. They are there to guide you in your role and support you on your personal journey to success. They shape our culture and support us in achieving our vision together, as one global team.

The Role

Our Editors review and edit a wide range of content outputs (including manuscripts, abstracts, posters, slides, PDFs, and digital materials) for grammar, spelling, consistency, and clarity while ensuring alignment with house, client and journal style guides. They apply consistent and appropriate use of digital markup tools, tracked changes and comments to provide clear, actionable editorial feedback.

They contribute to effective and timely project delivery by performing dummy submissions, ensuring the team is aware of specific requirements related to journal and congress guidelines. They proactively communicate and collaborate with internal teams to ensure best practices are being followed.

The right candidate will have impeccable English spelling, punctuation and grammar skills, and will display meticulous attention to detail.

  • Reviewing and editing a wide range of content outputs (including manuscripts, abstracts, posters, slides, PDFs, digital materials) for grammar, spelling, consistency, and clarity.

  • Proofing typeset copy to include consideration of layout (figures/tables, colors, size, quality, and resolution) and liaise with studio and/or journal for necessary amends.
  • Checking redrawn figures, PowerPoint and PDFs from studio to ensure accuracy versus submitted materials.

  • Recording and monitoring actual vs. budgeted time on projects and completing timesheets accurately each week, submitting by the deadline.
  • Proactively flagging when task scope, timelines, or budgets are misaligned.

  • Highest standards of English spelling, punctuation, and grammar
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Solutions-focused, sound judgement and problem-solving abilities
  • Ability to effectively work in a fast-paced agency setting
  • Strong multi-tasking, planning and organizational skills
  • Proficiency in Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Adobe Acrobat, EndNote, Outlook, Teams and SharePoint
  • Experience with digital markup, tracked changes, and editing tools
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Openness to learning, feedback and career development

Benefits

  • Supplemental medical, dental and vision insurance plans
  • Competitive salary
  • Generous time off
  • Pension

About us

LifeMD is a leading provider of virtual primary care, telehealth, and specialized treatment programs serving hundreds of thousands of patients nationwide. Our vertically integrated platform combines 50-state licensed providers, in-house pharmacy and lab integrations, and proprietary technology that enables safe, high-quality, and affordable care.

At the heart of this transformation is our team of developers, engineers, and tech innovators building state-of-the-art systems that make healthcare smarter, faster, and more accessible. From architecting scalable backend systems to crafting intuitive user experiences, we are pushing boundaries every day.

Recognized as one of the fastest-growing healthcare tech companies (#166 on Deloitte Fast 500 in 2023), LifeMD is not just a healthcare company â it's a tech company revolutionizing healthcare.

About the role

LifeMD is seeking a strategic, data-obsessed Director of Customer Experience to lead and elevate our remote customer operations. This role sits at the intersection of technology, clinical empathy, and operational excellence. We are looking for someone who has built and continuously evolved high-performing, technology-enabled CX organizations; deploying AI voice and chat tools, engineering data-driven performance cultures, and creating differentiated, concierge-level experiences that drive loyalty and growth.

Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations & Patient Experience, you will translate the executive team's vision and strategy into operational reality,surfacing the voice of the customer, driving measurable performance, and partnering cross-functionally to embed customer insights into decisions across the organization. If you thrive in fast-moving health tech environments and believe exceptional customer experience is a commercial advantage, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities

Remote Contact Center Leadership

  • Lead, scale, and continuously optimize a remote contact center team across multiple channels (voice, chat, email, SMS). Setting KPIs, driving performance expectations, and driving continuous improvement.
  • Set and enforce service level standards, workforce management practices, scheduling, capacity models, and escalation protocols
  • Build a high-accountability, coaching-first culture across team leads and frontline agents

Customer Experience

  • Develop and maintain service blueprints and experience standards across contact and service touchpoints that transform support from a transactional function into a driver of loyalty and advocacy
  • Champion a culture of empathy, accountability, and customer-centricity across the entire CX organization

AI & Technology Integration

  • Own the performance of AI-powered support functions including AI voice (conversational IVR), chatbots, and agent-assist tools â monitoring deflection rates, containment quality, sentiment signals, and escalation patterns
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to evaluate, implement, and iterate on AI tooling that augments agent performance and improves resolution rates without sacrificing human connection
  • Ensure deep integration between CX technology and broader customer-facing platforms including EHR, CRM, and marketing automation systems
  • â¢ Stay current on emerging customer support technologies and serve as the internal subject matter expert on responsible AI use within a healthcare context

Data-Driven Performance Management

  • Define, track, and improve core CX metrics: first contact resolution, average handle time, CSAT, NPS, escalation rate, AI containment rate, retention, and reactivation
  • Monitor NPS trends surfaced through the CX function and partner with the Manager of Patient Experience to close the loop on customer feedback and drive operational improvements
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reporting cadences that provide real-time operational visibility to your team and to the SVP
  • Conduct root cause analysis on performance gaps and translate findings into structured improvement plans
  • Synthesize customer insights, VOC data, and operational trends into clear, executive-ready briefings

Commercial Impact & Customer Lifecycle

  • Align CX operations with revenue and retention goals, connecting CSAT, NPS, and resolution metrics to commercial outcomes including retention, upsell conversion, and reactivation
  • Identify patterns in customer friction that represent risk to renewal, referral, or acquisition, and advocate for fixes cross-functionally
  • Support onboarding and activation workflows that reduce time-to-value; contribute to behavioral engagement and churn prediction strategies

Quality Assurance

  • Design and maintain a rigorous QA framework covering interaction quality, compliance, empathy standards, and clinical accuracy
  • Establish calibration processes across QA reviewers to ensure scoring consistency and fairness
  • Use QA insights to inform targeted coaching, training curricula, and process improvement

Budget Management

  • Manage the CX department budget within parameters, including headcount planning, vendor contracts, and technology spend
  • Identify cost optimization opportunities without compromising service quality or customer outcomes; present trade-off analyses and recommendations

Remote Transition & Operational Build-Out

  • Lead the operational transition to a fully remote customer service model, owning the end-to-end migration across people, process, technology, and compliance workstreams
  • Partner with HR, IT, Legal, and Operations to execute the transition with minimal disruption to the customer experience, establishing remote workforce policies and tooling standards
  • Use the transition as an opportunity to redesign foundational processes and eliminate legacy inefficiencies

Team Leadership & Development

  • Recruit, develop, and retain a high-performing team of managers, team leads, QA specialists, trainers, and agents
  • Build workforce planning, career pathing, and succession pipelines within the CX organization
  • Design the management rhythms, coaching frameworks, and recognition programs that attract and retain top talent in a fully remote environment

Cross-Functional Partnership & Internal Alignment

  • Serve as a key operational partner to the Manager of Patient Experience, ensuring alignment between customer-facing service operations and the broader patient experience program
  • Collaborate closely with the Manager of Patient Experience to align on messaging touchpoints, technology integrations, and shared data â recognizing that the customer journey spans both functions and requires active coordination to deliver a coherent experience
  • Support the SVP of Operations & Patient Experience in executing the overall CX vision, roadmap, and resource planning
  • Collaborate with Product, Clinical, Marketing, Sales, and Finance to embed the customer perspective in upstream decisions
  • Prepare structured insights, trend analyses, and investment recommendations for the SVP to carry into executive forums

Requirements

  • 7+ years of progressive CX, contact center, or customer operations leadership experience, with direct people management responsibility
  • Demonstrated experience leading remote or distributed teams of 50 or more across multiple channels and functions
  • Hands-on experience implementing or managing AI/automation in a customer service context (chatbots, conversational IVR, agent-assist tools)
  • Strong analytical skills â comfortable building dashboards, interpreting performance data, and translating insights into operational action
  • Proven track record connecting CX performance to commercial outcomes including retention, reactivation, and revenue
  • Experience managing vendor relationships including BPO partners and technology providers
  • Experience building or maturing QA programs in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment
  • Demonstrated ability to manage a department budget, including headcount, vendor, and technology spend

Preferred

  • Background in health tech, digital health, telehealth, or healthcare services
  • Familiarity with HIPAA requirements as they apply to CX operations, technology platforms, and data handling
  • Experience with platforms such as Salesforce Service Cloud, Zendesk, Five9, Genesys, or similar CRM/WFM tools
  • Exposure to customer and patient experience frameworks (e.g., service blueprinting, NPS program design, churn prediction models)
  • Background in a direct-to-consumer or subscription-based business where CX plays a direct role in lifetime value

Benefits

  • Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Retirement Plans
  • Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
  • Flexible PTO Policy
  • Paid Holidays
  • Short Term Disability
  • Training & Development

User Experience Designer

Full-time

LOCATION

Remote and HQ in Edinburgh when required

Overview

Weâre looking for a UX Designer who thrives on solving complex problems and making digital experiences feel effortless. You care about clarity, usability, and reducing friction â not just shipping pretty screens.

This role sits at the heart of how users engage with Caledonia. Youâll shape flows, build systems, and help turn financial services into something people actually enjoy using.

If you think like a designer but move like a product builder, we want to talk.

What You'll Do

  • Design end-to-end user experiences across web and mobile products
  • Collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, and stakeholders to shape feature direction and UX priorities
  • Translate product requirements into wireframes, prototypes, and detailed visual designs
  • Run user research, usability testing, and iterate based on real feedback
  • Develop and maintain UX patterns and documentation to ensure consistency
  • Help define and evolve the design language and component library
  • Present design decisions clearly and advocate for user needs in every conversation

What You'll Bring

  • 3 or more years of experience in UX, interaction design, or product design
  • A strong portfolio that shows how you solve real-world problems through design
  • Proven experience designing digital products, not just landing pages or marketing sites
  • Excellent understanding of design tools like Figma, along with prototyping and handoff workflows
  • Comfortable working alongside engineers and product managers in agile teams
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to explain design thinking clearly
  • A mindset of constant learning, with a sharp eye for detail and improvement

Caledonia is a next-generation financial company focused on serving freelancers, creators, and independent professionals. Weâre building adaptive, AI-powered banking infrastructure that challenges the legacy systems of the past.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description: At AlixPartners, we tackle complex challenges by transforming insights into innovative solutions, delivering lasting value for businesses, their people, and the communities they serve. Our products are designed to drive meaningful impact, ensuring sustainable growth and success. By understanding, respecting, and honoring the needs of our employees, clients, and communities, AlixPartners actively promotes an inclusive environment. We strongly believe in the value that diversity of thoughts and experiences bring to our firm, and are committed to the perpetual enhancement of initiatives, policies, and practices. We hold ourselves accountable by providing the space for authenticity, growth, and equity for everyone. AlixPartners has embraced a hybrid work model to provide flexibility and support our employees' work-life integration. Our hybrid model combines a mix of in-person and remote working. This role follows a different cadence to traditional consulting or on-site client presence. It follows a traditional product development cadence, while being expected to engage our users in appropriate situations such as business conferences and in-person workshops. What you'll do As Product Marketing Manager at AlixPartners, your primary responsibility is to own and manage the marketing programs around the firmâs growing portfolio of technology products. These are typically used on client engagements, and a large part of the role is driving internal awareness, adoption, and engagement across practitioners and client-facing teams. You will translate complex capabilities into clear value narratives, building internal and external marketing programs This role spans the full Platforms portfolio, with responsibility for raising awareness holistically across all products and initiatives, not just individual releases. You will work hand-in-hand with the Product Manager and cross-functional stakeholders to turn feature releases into awareness moments, and usage gaps into engagement campaigns. Key Responsibilities Product Branding and Content Development. Partner with Product Managers, industry and service lines, and the wider marketing team to define the market-facing identity of each product in the Platforms portfolio. Establish and maintain clear value propositions, positioning statements, and messaging frameworks aligned with the firm's wider brand proposition and visual identity standards. Lead the productization process â translating product capabilities into market-ready narratives. Brief and direct creative teams on product naming, visual identity, and brand standards. Drive the development of core go-to-market content, including digital assets and sales material, ensuring a cohesive product presence before and beyond any individual launch. Create high-quality product content including demos, feature walkthroughs, onboarding materials, and release announcements. Concept, brief and direct agency/contractors to produce video content to a professional standard. Maintain and improve internal knowledge bases, wiki pages, and public-facing product pages to ensure content stays current and accurate. Internal Product Promotion and Awareness Build and execute internal marketing campaigns that drive product visibility, feature adoption, and top-of-mind awareness across business units and geographies. Ensure consistent messaging across channels. This includes firm-wide awareness initiatives that promote the Platforms portfolio as a whole, beyond individual product launches. Product Demos and Showcases Deliver live and recorded product demonstrations for internal stakeholders, new internal users, and leadership. Present new features in a way that connects directly to user needs and business outcomes. Stakeholder Engagement Build relationships with key stakeholders across the firm. Understand their workflows, pain points, and communication preferences. Translate that knowledge into targeted campaigns that resonate with specific user groups. Marketing Collaboration Serve as the primary bridge between the Platforms product team and the central marketing function, operating with a close dotted-line relationship to the marketing team. Co-develop campaigns, align on messaging, and coordinate on external and firm-wide product promotions. Ensure all firm-wide communications follow established marketing protocols and channel ownership. Strategy and Playbook Development Develop a structured awareness and adoption strategy for the Platforms portfolio. Build repeatable playbooks that can be applied across products and scaled as the portfolio grows. Translate strategy into actionable plans with clear milestones and ownership. Feedback Collection and PM Partnership Act as a structured channel for user feedback. Gather insights from campaigns, demos, and stakeholder conversations, and bring them back to the Product Manager as actionable input. Serve as a close partner to the PM throughout the product lifecycle. Automation and Tooling Build and maintain marketing automation workflows using Power Automate or similar tools to scale communication efforts, manage campaign triggers, and reduce manual overhead. Metrics and Performance Define and track engagement metrics tied to awareness and adoption goals. Report on campaign effectiveness and continuously refine approach based on data. This description is not designed to encompass a comprehensive listing of required activities, duties, or responsibilities. What you'll need Minimum of 6 years of relevant Product Marketing or Product Management experience. Proven track record of building and executing internal or Enterprise B2B marketing campaigns with measurable results. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English. Able to communicate complex product concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Comfortable presenting and demoing products to diverse audiences, including senior leadership. Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with experience working alongside Product and Engineering teams. Analytical mindset with experience defining and tracking KPIs for awareness and adoption programs. Demonstrated ability to build marketing strategies and repeatable playbooks in complex, multi-product environments. Intellectual curiosity and a commitment to ongoing personal and professional development. Experience building automation workflows using AI (Power Automate, Zapier, or equivalent tools - Nice to Have). Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field preferred. Plus: 2+ years of experience in a professional services or consulting firm environment. The firm offers a comprehensive benefits program including health, vision, dental, disability, 401K, tuition reimbursement, identity theft protection, and mental wellness support. Employees will also receive a generous paid leave policy. The salary range for this role takes into account a number of factors and is between $120,000/year - $220,000/year with eligibility for an annual discretionary bonus. AlixPartners is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, among other things, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, status as a protected veteran, or disability. AlixPartners is a proud Gold award-winning Veteran Friendly Employer. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. raw_payload.description:
Description

Overview:

Red Rover is seeking an organized, proactive, and eager-to-learn budding marketer or early-career marketing professional to support the execution, coordination, and day-to-day operations of our growing marketing organization as a Marketing Associate.

The Marketing Associate plays an important role in helping ongoing campaigns, programs, and initiatives stay organized, execute successfully, and remain aligned across marketing and cross-functional teams.

This role collaborates across teams, contributing to a wide variety of marketing initiatives and projects. Working alongside experienced marketing leaders, the Marketing Associate will build a broad foundation across campaign marketing, product marketing, content strategy, customer marketing, field marketing and events, sales enablement, and go-to-market execution while helping the team operate more efficiently as Red Rover continues to grow.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, collaborative, and detail-oriented, and enjoys variety, continuous learning, and fast-moving projects. They're eager to gain hands-on experience across all aspects of modern B2B SaaS marketing.

What Youâll Do

Marketing campaign & program support

  • Support the planning, coordination, and execution of integrated marketing campaigns and strategic initiatives across multiple marketing programs
  • Assist with email campaign preparation and scheduling, webinar coordination and preparation, campaign timelines, promotional communications, marketing calendar coordination, campaign asset coordination, website & CRM management, and cross-functional coordination
  • Help ensure campaigns remain organized, on schedule, and aligned across marketing and sales teams

Cross-functional coordination & team support

  • Help coordinate projects, communication, and day-to-day marketing initiatives across sales, SDR, and marketing teams
  • Support activities including project timeline management, meeting preparation, action item tracking, workflow coordination, internal communications, marketing request management, project documentation, team follow-up

Event & field marketing support

  • Support the planning and execution of webinars, conferences, customer events, regional marketing initiatives, and field marketing programs alongside marketing team
  • Assist with webinar event logistics, registration management, presentation and speaker coordination, promotional campaigns and communications, sales coordination, post-event follow-ups, etc.
  • Assist with strategic planning and onsite execution logistics for tradeshows, conferences, and regional events
  • Help contribute to memorable customer and prospect experiences before, during, and after each event

Content & marketing asset coordination

  • Support the marketing organization in publishing and maintaining marketing content library and sales resources across multiple channels
  • Assist with blog publishing, marketing asset organization, webinar materials, sales collateral materials, digital asset management, social media scheduling, website content coordination, and content library management

Marketing operations & team organization

  • Help maintain the operational foundation that keeps the marketing organization running efficiently
  • Support activities including project tracking, campaign organization, campaign performance reporting support, workflow management, budget tracking assistance, tradeshow and events calendar management, etc.
  • Assist in marketing database updates and campaign and program builds alongside marketing operations team

Professional growth & continuous learning

  • Take an active role in developing marketing knowledge and expanding level of responsibilities over time
  • Demonstrate curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to continuously improve and learn while eager to build experience and deepen knowledge across demand generation, campaign marketing, product marketing, brand marketing, content strategy, customer marketing and advocacy, field marketing and events, marketing operations, go-to-market strategy, and AI and traditional or emerging marketing technologies

Requirements

Qualifications:

  • 0-3 years of experience in marketing, communications, business, customer-facing roles, events, or related fields
  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or related field preferred
  • Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail, proven project management skills preferred
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Positive attitude with a willingness to learn and take initiative
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, collaborative environment
  • Strong follow-through and reliability
  • Comfortable working cross-functionally with multiple teams
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office and SharePoint/OneDrive
  • Experience with Canva, HubSpot, or similar marketing platforms and tools is a plus
  • Interest in SaaS, education technology, or B2B marketing environments preferred
  • Ability to travel 15-20% to attend department summits, company events, and regional/sales events

Bonus Skills

  • Experience supporting marketing campaigns, events, or social media initiatives
  • Familiarity with email marketing platforms or marketing automation tools
  • Basic graphic design experience using Canva or Adobe Express
  • Experience with project management platforms such as Asana, Monday.com, or Airtable
  • Experience writing or editing marketing content
  • Interest in AI tools that improve marketing productivity and execution
  • Exposure to CRM platforms such as HubSpot or Salesforce
  • Experience working with K-12 education or other mission-driven organizations

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators. It will begin with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $75 - $120 p/hr pending seniority & experience. This position offers strong growth potential for the right candidate, including opportunities for advancement within the Accounting team or other departments.

This is a remote role for candidates located in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. 

About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $100M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services — operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

About Engineering at LawnStarter

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

 

The Role

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work calls for careful, hand-written code in a sensitive area, you write it yourself.

What makes this role exciting:

  • You ship end-to-end. From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
  • You work as a true product partner. You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
  • You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints. You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.
  • You operate at a staff bar. You're trusted to make the call, ship the hard thing, and stand behind the outcome.

 

What You'll Own

 

  • The technical approach — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
  • Implementation quality — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
  • Cross-functional partnership — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
  • The initiative outcome — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
  • A high bar for what ships — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

 

Problems to Solve

 

Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

Owning decisions with high autonomy You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

Shipping outcomes, not features Each initiative is measured by a metric — a conversion rate, a retention curve, a pro-funnel KPI, a unit-economics shift. You're accountable for the number alongside your team. How do you scope to actually move it, decide what *not* to build, and have the discipline to follow up 2–4 weeks after launch?

 

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

 

  • Initiative outcomes hit — You've shipped 3–4 initiatives end-to-end, and at least two clearly moved their metric (with the post-launch review to prove it).
  • Agent workflow that travels — The prompts, evals, and review loop you built are picked up by peers on other initiatives.
  • Faster cycle time — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
  • Quality holds — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.
  • Visible leverage — Peers point to artifacts you left behind — runbooks, evals, agent workflows, post-launch write-ups — as references they use.



Requirements

Who You Are

 

  • AI-native. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent are how you ship today — daily, on production work. You have real opinions about prompts, evals, agent loops, and review workflows, and you know when to let the agent run versus write it yourself.
  • Operating at a lead level. Whatever your current title, you've been the person making the call, shipping the hard thing, and standing behind whether it worked.
  • Outcome-driven. You measure your week in "did the metric move" and "did the experience get better." You read the post-launch dashboard and own the answer.
  • A strong horizontal partner. You hold your own with a strong PM and designer, and you collaborate well with engineering peers in a shared codebase. You bring engineering judgment to product calls and product judgment to engineering calls.
  • Decisive and documented. You make architecture, data-model, and rollout calls, write them down, get fast input, and move.
  • A force multiplier. Your impact compounds beyond your own initiative because you leave reusable artifacts behind — agent workflows, evals, runbooks, post-launch reviews.
  • Customer- and pro-minded. This is a real marketplace with real people on both sides, and you care about the outcomes for both.

 

Good to Know

 

  • An individual-contributor role with room to grow. People management sits with the EM — but the path into management is an open door for those who want it.
  • A product-engineering role, end-to-end. You ship features that move metrics; platform and architecture work happen inside the initiative when the outcome needs them.
  • Hands-on, with a high quality bar. Agents handle much of the implementation; you bring the judgment, design, safety, and accountability. The bar is high.
  • Shipping to a live marketplace. With $100M+ in bookings, customers and pros use what you ship within the same week.

 

Tech You'll Touch

 

  • AI agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, internal agent stack, MCP servers, evals tooling
  • Backend — PHP/Laravel
  • Frontend — TypeScript/React/React Native (customer & pro apps, web and mobile)
  • Data — Redshift, dbt, Segment, Airflow
  • Infra — AWS, Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions
  • Documentation & process — Brain (Claude Code skills + docs repo), Confluence, Jira

You don't need every box checked. You need deep skill in at least one of our stacks plus credible production experience with AI coding agents.



Benefits

  • Competitive salary of USD $80,000–$100,000 annual base
  • Work from anywhere
  • High ownership and autonomy
  • Fast-moving team that loves to build, learn, and grow

This is a remote role for candidates located in Campinas, Brazil.

 

About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $100M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services — operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

About Engineering at LawnStarter

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

 

The Role

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work calls for careful, hand-written code in a sensitive area, you write it yourself.

What makes this role exciting:

  • You ship end-to-end. From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
  • You work as a true product partner. You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
  • You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints. You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.
  • You operate at a staff bar. You're trusted to make the call, ship the hard thing, and stand behind the outcome.

 

What You'll Own

 

  • The technical approach — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
  • Implementation quality — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
  • Cross-functional partnership — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
  • The initiative outcome — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
  • A high bar for what ships — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

 

Problems to Solve

 

Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

Owning decisions with high autonomy You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

Shipping outcomes, not features Each initiative is measured by a metric — a conversion rate, a retention curve, a pro-funnel KPI, a unit-economics shift. You're accountable for the number alongside your team. How do you scope to actually move it, decide what *not* to build, and have the discipline to follow up 2–4 weeks after launch?

 

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

 

  • Initiative outcomes hit — You've shipped 3–4 initiatives end-to-end, and at least two clearly moved their metric (with the post-launch review to prove it).
  • Agent workflow that travels — The prompts, evals, and review loop you built are picked up by peers on other initiatives.
  • Faster cycle time — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
  • Quality holds — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.
  • Visible leverage — Peers point to artifacts you left behind — runbooks, evals, agent workflows, post-launch write-ups — as references they use.



Requirements

Who You Are

 

  • AI-native. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent are how you ship today — daily, on production work. You have real opinions about prompts, evals, agent loops, and review workflows, and you know when to let the agent run versus write it yourself.
  • Operating at a lead level. Whatever your current title, you've been the person making the call, shipping the hard thing, and standing behind whether it worked.
  • Outcome-driven. You measure your week in "did the metric move" and "did the experience get better." You read the post-launch dashboard and own the answer.
  • A strong horizontal partner. You hold your own with a strong PM and designer, and you collaborate well with engineering peers in a shared codebase. You bring engineering judgment to product calls and product judgment to engineering calls.
  • Decisive and documented. You make architecture, data-model, and rollout calls, write them down, get fast input, and move.
  • A force multiplier. Your impact compounds beyond your own initiative because you leave reusable artifacts behind — agent workflows, evals, runbooks, post-launch reviews.
  • Customer- and pro-minded. This is a real marketplace with real people on both sides, and you care about the outcomes for both.

 

Good to Know

 

  • An individual-contributor role with room to grow. People management sits with the EM — but the path into management is an open door for those who want it.
  • A product-engineering role, end-to-end. You ship features that move metrics; platform and architecture work happen inside the initiative when the outcome needs them.
  • Hands-on, with a high quality bar. Agents handle much of the implementation; you bring the judgment, design, safety, and accountability. The bar is high.
  • Shipping to a live marketplace. With $100M+ in bookings, customers and pros use what you ship within the same week.

 

Tech You'll Touch

 

  • AI agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, internal agent stack, MCP servers, evals tooling
  • Backend — PHP/Laravel
  • Frontend — TypeScript/React/React Native (customer & pro apps, web and mobile)
  • Data — Redshift, dbt, Segment, Airflow
  • Infra — AWS, Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions
  • Documentation & process — Brain (Claude Code skills + docs repo), Confluence, Jira

You don't need every box checked. You need deep skill in at least one of our stacks plus credible production experience with AI coding agents.



Benefits

  • Competitive salary of USD $80,000–$100,000 annual base
  • Work from anywhere
  • High ownership and autonomy
  • Fast-moving team that loves to build, learn, and grow

This is a remote role for candidates located in Mexico City, Mexico.

 

About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $100M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services — operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

About Engineering at LawnStarter

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

 

The Role

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work calls for careful, hand-written code in a sensitive area, you write it yourself.

What makes this role exciting:

  • You ship end-to-end. From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
  • You work as a true product partner. You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
  • You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints. You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.
  • You operate at a staff bar. You're trusted to make the call, ship the hard thing, and stand behind the outcome.

 

What You'll Own

 

  • The technical approach — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
  • Implementation quality — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
  • Cross-functional partnership — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
  • The initiative outcome — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
  • A high bar for what ships — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

 

Problems to Solve

 

Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

Owning decisions with high autonomy You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

Shipping outcomes, not features Each initiative is measured by a metric — a conversion rate, a retention curve, a pro-funnel KPI, a unit-economics shift. You're accountable for the number alongside your team. How do you scope to actually move it, decide what *not* to build, and have the discipline to follow up 2–4 weeks after launch?

 

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

 

  • Initiative outcomes hit — You've shipped 3–4 initiatives end-to-end, and at least two clearly moved their metric (with the post-launch review to prove it).
  • Agent workflow that travels — The prompts, evals, and review loop you built are picked up by peers on other initiatives.
  • Faster cycle time — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
  • Quality holds — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.
  • Visible leverage — Peers point to artifacts you left behind — runbooks, evals, agent workflows, post-launch write-ups — as references they use.



Requirements

Who You Are

 

  • AI-native. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent are how you ship today — daily, on production work. You have real opinions about prompts, evals, agent loops, and review workflows, and you know when to let the agent run versus write it yourself.
  • Operating at a lead level. Whatever your current title, you've been the person making the call, shipping the hard thing, and standing behind whether it worked.
  • Outcome-driven. You measure your week in "did the metric move" and "did the experience get better." You read the post-launch dashboard and own the answer.
  • A strong horizontal partner. You hold your own with a strong PM and designer, and you collaborate well with engineering peers in a shared codebase. You bring engineering judgment to product calls and product judgment to engineering calls.
  • Decisive and documented. You make architecture, data-model, and rollout calls, write them down, get fast input, and move.
  • A force multiplier. Your impact compounds beyond your own initiative because you leave reusable artifacts behind — agent workflows, evals, runbooks, post-launch reviews.
  • Customer- and pro-minded. This is a real marketplace with real people on both sides, and you care about the outcomes for both.

 

Good to Know

 

  • An individual-contributor role with room to grow. People management sits with the EM — but the path into management is an open door for those who want it.
  • A product-engineering role, end-to-end. You ship features that move metrics; platform and architecture work happen inside the initiative when the outcome needs them.
  • Hands-on, with a high quality bar. Agents handle much of the implementation; you bring the judgment, design, safety, and accountability. The bar is high.
  • Shipping to a live marketplace. With $100M+ in bookings, customers and pros use what you ship within the same week.

 

Tech You'll Touch

 

  • AI agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, internal agent stack, MCP servers, evals tooling
  • Backend — PHP/Laravel
  • Frontend — TypeScript/React/React Native (customer & pro apps, web and mobile)
  • Data — Redshift, dbt, Segment, Airflow
  • Infra — AWS, Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions
  • Documentation & process — Brain (Claude Code skills + docs repo), Confluence, Jira

You don't need every box checked. You need deep skill in at least one of our stacks plus credible production experience with AI coding agents.



Benefits

  • Competitive salary of USD $80,000–$100,000 annual base
  • Work from anywhere
  • High ownership and autonomy
  • Fast-moving team that loves to build, learn, and grow

This is a remote role for candidates located in Campinas, Brazil.

 

About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $100M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services — operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

About Engineering at LawnStarter

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

 

The Role

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work calls for careful, hand-written code in a sensitive area, you write it yourself.

What makes this role exciting:

  • You ship end-to-end. From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
  • You work as a true product partner. You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
  • You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints. You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.
  • You operate at a staff bar. You're trusted to make the call, ship the hard thing, and stand behind the outcome.

 

What You'll Own

 

  • The technical approach — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
  • Implementation quality — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
  • Cross-functional partnership — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
  • The initiative outcome — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
  • A high bar for what ships — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

 

Problems to Solve

 

Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

Owning decisions with high autonomy You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

Shipping outcomes, not features Each initiative is measured by a metric — a conversion rate, a retention curve, a pro-funnel KPI, a unit-economics shift. You're accountable for the number alongside your team. How do you scope to actually move it, decide what *not* to build, and have the discipline to follow up 2–4 weeks after launch?

 

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

 

  • Initiative outcomes hit — You've shipped 3–4 initiatives end-to-end, and at least two clearly moved their metric (with the post-launch review to prove it).
  • Agent workflow that travels — The prompts, evals, and review loop you built are picked up by peers on other initiatives.
  • Faster cycle time — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
  • Quality holds — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.
  • Visible leverage — Peers point to artifacts you left behind — runbooks, evals, agent workflows, post-launch write-ups — as references they use.



Requirements

Who You Are

 

  • AI-native. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent are how you ship today — daily, on production work. You have real opinions about prompts, evals, agent loops, and review workflows, and you know when to let the agent run versus write it yourself.
  • Operating at a lead level. Whatever your current title, you've been the person making the call, shipping the hard thing, and standing behind whether it worked.
  • Outcome-driven. You measure your week in "did the metric move" and "did the experience get better." You read the post-launch dashboard and own the answer.
  • A strong horizontal partner. You hold your own with a strong PM and designer, and you collaborate well with engineering peers in a shared codebase. You bring engineering judgment to product calls and product judgment to engineering calls.
  • Decisive and documented. You make architecture, data-model, and rollout calls, write them down, get fast input, and move.
  • A force multiplier. Your impact compounds beyond your own initiative because you leave reusable artifacts behind — agent workflows, evals, runbooks, post-launch reviews.
  • Customer- and pro-minded. This is a real marketplace with real people on both sides, and you care about the outcomes for both.

 

Good to Know

 

  • An individual-contributor role with room to grow. People management sits with the EM — but the path into management is an open door for those who want it.
  • A product-engineering role, end-to-end. You ship features that move metrics; platform and architecture work happen inside the initiative when the outcome needs them.
  • Hands-on, with a high quality bar. Agents handle much of the implementation; you bring the judgment, design, safety, and accountability. The bar is high.
  • Shipping to a live marketplace. With $100M+ in bookings, customers and pros use what you ship within the same week.

 

Tech You'll Touch

 

  • AI agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, internal agent stack, MCP servers, evals tooling
  • Backend — PHP/Laravel
  • Frontend — TypeScript/React/React Native (customer & pro apps, web and mobile)
  • Data — Redshift, dbt, Segment, Airflow
  • Infra — AWS, Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions
  • Documentation & process — Brain (Claude Code skills + docs repo), Confluence, Jira

You don't need every box checked. You need deep skill in at least one of our stacks plus credible production experience with AI coding agents.



Benefits

  • Competitive salary of USD $80,000–$100,000 annual base
  • Work from anywhere
  • High ownership and autonomy
  • Fast-moving team that loves to build, learn, and grow

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

 

The Role

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work calls for careful, hand-written code in a sensitive area, you write it yourself.

What makes this role exciting:

  • You ship end-to-end. From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
  • You work as a true product partner. You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
  • You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints. You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.
  • You operate at a staff bar. You're trusted to make the call, ship the hard thing, and stand behind the outcome.

 

What You'll Own

 

  • The technical approach — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
  • Implementation quality — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
  • Cross-functional partnership — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
  • The initiative outcome — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
  • A high bar for what ships — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

 

Problems to Solve

 

Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

Owning decisions with high autonomy You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

Shipping outcomes, not features Each initiative is measured by a metric — a conversion rate, a retention curve, a pro-funnel KPI, a unit-economics shift. You're accountable for the number alongside your team. How do you scope to actually move it, decide what *not* to build, and have the discipline to follow up 2–4 weeks after launch?

 

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

 

  • Initiative outcomes hit — You've shipped 3–4 initiatives end-to-end, and at least two clearly moved their metric (with the post-launch review to prove it).
  • Agent workflow that travels — The prompts, evals, and review loop you built are picked up by peers on other initiatives.
  • Faster cycle time — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
  • Quality holds — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.
  • Visible leverage — Peers point to artifacts you left behind — runbooks, evals, agent workflows, post-launch write-ups — as references they use.



Requirements

Who You Are

 

  • AI-native. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent are how you ship today — daily, on production work. You have real opinions about prompts, evals, agent loops, and review workflows, and you know when to let the agent run versus write it yourself.
  • Operating at a lead level. Whatever your current title, you've been the person making the call, shipping the hard thing, and standing behind whether it worked.
  • Outcome-driven. You measure your week in "did the metric move" and "did the experience get better." You read the post-launch dashboard and own the answer.
  • A strong horizontal partner. You hold your own with a strong PM and designer, and you collaborate well with engineering peers in a shared codebase. You bring engineering judgment to product calls and product judgment to engineering calls.
  • Decisive and documented. You make architecture, data-model, and rollout calls, write them down, get fast input, and move.
  • A force multiplier. Your impact compounds beyond your own initiative because you leave reusable artifacts behind — agent workflows, evals, runbooks, post-launch reviews.
  • Customer- and pro-minded. This is a real marketplace with real people on both sides, and you care about the outcomes for both.

 

Good to Know

 

  • An individual-contributor role with room to grow. People management sits with the EM — but the path into management is an open door for those who want it.
  • A product-engineering role, end-to-end. You ship features that move metrics; platform and architecture work happen inside the initiative when the outcome needs them.
  • Hands-on, with a high quality bar. Agents handle much of the implementation; you bring the judgment, design, safety, and accountability. The bar is high.
  • Shipping to a live marketplace. With $100M+ in bookings, customers and pros use what you ship within the same week.

 

Tech You'll Touch

 

  • AI agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, internal agent stack, MCP servers, evals tooling
  • Backend — PHP/Laravel
  • Frontend — TypeScript/React/React Native (customer & pro apps, web and mobile)
  • Data — Redshift, dbt, Segment, Airflow
  • Infra — AWS, Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions
  • Documentation & process — Brain (Claude Code skills + docs repo), Confluence, Jira

You don't need every box checked. You need deep skill in at least one of our stacks plus credible production experience with AI coding agents.



Benefits

  • Competitive salary of USD $80,000–$100,000 annual base
  • Work from anywhere
  • High ownership and autonomy
  • Fast-moving team that loves to build, learn, and grow

What you’ll do TSEs understand the fundamentals of programming incredibly well and eagerly jump in and familiarize themselves with others’ code. You will do a wide variety of things, including explaining technical concepts about Stripe’s products, build and debug integrations with developers, and produce/improve guides that help our users solve particular problems to be successful with Stripe. You will interact with developers of all skill levels through a variety of mediums, enabling them to be successful when using Stripe. Early on, current team members will devote a large amount of time to teaching you and helping you get to a level of comfort and expertise with Stripe, its services, and how we interact with users. Later, we’d love for you to take on this role with others on the team and Stripes broadly, as teaching is a great way to learn and to reinforce what you know. If you’re someone who enjoys working with all kinds of code, is a fast researcher, a strong writer, and enthusiastic about helping others build mission-critical products with Stripe, we want to hear from you! Unblock external developers with their thorniest integration challenges through a variety of support channels including email, ticketing software, internal issue trackers, community platforms (like StackOverflow), and real-time chat software (like Slack and Discord) Develop and maintain internal and external documentation, examples, integration demos, and code-snippets that demonstrate usage patterns of the Stripe infrastructure. Identify points of friction developers encounter and collaborate with engineering teams to make Stripe products better. Participate in a number of extended engineering teams’ regular planning sessions, design reviews, and development meetings. Develop and maintain a suite of internal support tooling for TSE and Stripe Support more broadly e.g. a retrieval augmented generation LLM-based Copilot tool or the Invoice Explainer Admin tool. Act as a developer advocate and educational resource internal to the organization by regularly assembling training for non-developers internal to the organization and responding in real-time to product integration questions. Who you are We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. This role is remote but requires candidates to be located in the Mountain or Pacific time zones. Minimum requirements At least 4 years of full-stack software development experience, with a proven track record of building web or mobile applications that deliver high-quality user experiences Direct experience explaining technical concepts, and would be comfortable explaining how Stripe works to both technical and non-technical audiences Understands how to write good, clean code in multiple programming languages, as well as how to read code that might not be quite as well written Ability to help users during working hours in the region you are in. This may occasionally include providing weekend coverage for monitoring/supporting critical infrastructure, which TSEs are uniquely equipped to assist with given the team’s knowledge around Stripe’s products and active integrations. The team is largely remote, and we are very supportive of working arrangements that allow for family care and other needs to be met. Preferred qualifications Enjoys writing in a clear and quick manner General software engineering skills are important to us, as we understand that new languages and frameworks can be learned if you understand the concepts Experience teaching or coaching developers Comfort working with a great deal of autonomy and limited supervision Degree in Computer Science, Software/Computer Engineering, or a related analytical field of study To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/stripe-technical-solutions-engineer

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Data Platform team within the Platform group, you will help build the systems that centralize all of Coinbase's internal and third-party data. The Data Platform team makes it easy for teams across the company to access, process, and transform data for analytics, machine learning, and powering end-user experiences. You'll contribute to the full spectrum of our systems, from foundational data storage and processing to scalable pipelines, frameworks, and internal applications that make data efficiently available to every team at Coinbase.

What you'll do:

  • Own the design, development, and operation of foundational data services spanning cloud data warehouses, data lakes, orchestration (Airflow), batch processing (Spark, SQL), streaming (Kafka), query federation, and real-time event aggregation stores.
  • Build and maintain data integration and processing SDKs used by internal services and product teams throughout Coinbase to interact with the data platform reliably at scale.
  • Deliver self-service applications that empower users to manage, monitor, and troubleshoot their own data pipelines running on our platform infrastructure.
  • Architect end-to-end data security and observability services, including access controls across multiple storage and access layers, data quality tracking, dataset cataloging, lineage, and usage auditing.
  • Partner with data analysts, ML engineers, and security and compliance teams to convert functional requests into reusable, scalable patterns and assemble data microservices into platforms for critical business verticals.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 5+ years of experience in backend software engineering, with hands-on experience building and operating data systems or data pipelines in production.
  • Proficiency in Python, Go, or Java for backend development, with demonstrated ability to build services that process and serve data at scale.
  • Experience with data infrastructure patterns including scale-out architectures, caching layers, key/value stores, and columnar storage systems.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL, Airflow, Spark, Kafka, or similar data processing and orchestration frameworks in production environments.
  • Experience with data security, access control, or data observability systems, including cataloging, lineage, or quality monitoring.

jobs.description: Headquarters: New York City, Washington DC, Remote Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Deal Pricing is a dedicated global function that provides deal pricing expertise, financial insights, and deal support for negotiated users to Stripe's global Go-to-Market teams. We work to ensure deals create economic value for Stripe by establishing the deal commercial framework for a scaling sales organization, actively supporting large and strategic deals, and providing pricing insights and feedback to sales, finance, and product leaders. Deal Pricing frequently works with cross-functional business partners across Operations, Finance and Strategy, and Product. There is constant collaboration with Deal Pricing colleagues across all regions. Rather than pricing individual deals, this Strategy and Operations (S&O) role acts as a central engine behind the global deal pricing team. You’ll serve as a "Chief of Staff" function to Deal Pricing leadership—owning the global operating model, driving cross-functional process excellence, managing our strategic operating rhythm, and codifying our commercial knowledge so Stripe can scale its GTM velocity. What you’ll do Strategic planning and operating rhythm Drive strategy execution. Translate high-level annual goals into actionable quarterly OKRs, ensuring clear ownership and measurable progress. Manage the operating cadence. Facilitate the team’s operating rhythm (MBRs, QBRs, and leadership syncs) to drive accountability, surface risks, and unblock cross-functional dependencies. Strategic telemetry and insights. Collaborate with our tooling and analytics team to track functional performance, using data to inform pricing strategy, operational pivots, and executive decision-making. Commercial governance and friction management Optimize cross-functional SLAs. Act as the primary bridge between Sales velocity and risk-mitigation functions (Deal Strategy, Finance, Treasury). Define and enforce SLAs for deal pricing approvals to ensure global consistency. Resolve bottlenecks. Proactively identify process friction, working with partner ops teams to redesign playbooks and clarify decision-making boundaries. Knowledge infrastructure and sales enablement Codify the "Deal pricing playbook." Build and maintain a single source of truth for deal pricing frameworks, guidelines, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), ensuring documentation is version-controlled and highly discoverable. Scale sales self-service. Partner with Sales Enablement to translate complex commercial policies into self-serve guides and playbooks, empowering Sales to execute simple deals independently. Process and AI architecture Systems roadmap. Act as a lead for our CRM and CPQ evolution, transforming manual, spreadsheet-based pricing into automated, scalable workflows. Deploy AI for efficiency. Proactively identify and implement AI and LLM solutions to accelerate operations—including automating documentation, summarizing legacy contract terms, and extracting data from unstructured sales communications. Who you are We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 6–8+ years of experience in Business Operations (BizOps), Sales and Revenue Operations, Management Consulting, or a Chief of Staff role supporting a high-growth GTM team. Practical experience using generative AI tools (e.g., LLMs, advanced prompting techniques, AI-driven search/synthesis tools) to accelerate your work. While not a software engineer, you are “technically savvy.” You can navigate data structures and AI orchestration tools to build prototypes or initial solutions independently. Proven experience translating high-level corporate strategy into operational execution frameworks (OKRs, KPIs) Outstanding written communication skills. You must be able to write clear, structured, and highly professional playbooks and memos (critical for Stripe’s document-centric culture). A track record of mapping complex, cross-functional processes, identifying root causes of friction, and redesigning workflows to improve cycle times. Strong understanding of GTM tech stacks (Salesforce, CPQ, workflow automation) and how to write clear business requirement documents (BRDs) for technical teams. Preferred qualifications Experience in Fintech, Payments, or consumption-based (API) SaaS models. Direct experience building simple automation flows to optimize personal or team productivity. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/stripe-strategy-and-operations-lead-deal-pricing

Deal Pricing frequently works with cross-functional business partners across Operations, Finance and Strategy, and Product. There is constant collaboration with Deal Pricing colleagues across all regions.

Rather than pricing individual deals, this Strategy and Operations (S&O) role acts as a central engine behind the global deal pricing team.
